AI MATHEMATICAL DISCOVERY & INTERGENERATIONAL KNOWLEDGE EVOLUTION AT THE LIMIT A High-Density Research-Design Monograph on AI Reasoning, Formal Verification, and Mathematical Knowledge Succession STARLI | White Rainbow Civilization Mathematical Frontier Trilogy — Volume III Research-design edition | 13 October 2026 DESCRIPTION How can mathematical research remain inspectable, reproducible, corrigible, and useful to future generations when artificial intelligence participates in conjecture formation and proof discovery? This independently authored research-design monograph investigates this question through a three-component framework: AI Mathematical Reasoning × Formal Verification × Intergenerational Knowledge Evolution. Volume III completes a planned trilogy by shifting the focus from mathematical proof structures (Volume I) and cross-domain structural synthesis (Volume II) toward the institutions, formal artifacts, epistemic boundaries, and preservation methods needed for responsible AI-assisted mathematics. It proposes research protocols rather than claiming to establish new mathematical theorems. The monograph comprises 82 thematic chapters, each with one chapter-opening research relation and 12 individually paginated research units. Its six parts address: (I) research-oriented AI mathematical reasoning; (II) Lean, proof objects, and formal verification; (III) mathematician–AI collaboration and independent review; (IV) conjecture generation and counterexample search; (V) mathematical knowledge graphs, provenance, and proof archaeology; and (VI) long-term mathematical succession, model retirement, and open research governance. The final sections present 200 numbered Research Gates (G401–G600 in the trilogy-wide sequence) and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Research Gates are designed as executable entrances into unresolved work: each specifies an open question, a proposed test, an adversarial or stopping condition, and the evidence required for independent reassessment. The Answer Embryos are provisional research instruments that can be falsified, repaired, branched, or retired. A separate workbook indexes the chapters, research units, gates, candidate answers, and equation cards. The opening scientific preface contains 30 high-level physics derivation-route cards accompanied by conceptual three-dimensional geometric studies. Each of the 200 Research Gates and 33 Answer Embryos includes one distinct physics equation card, for a total of 233 equations. These retain their meaning within their original physical regimes; they are not presented as proofs of the book's claims about AI systems or mathematics. PRIMARY-SOURCE CONTEXT AND SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARIES The publicly available OpenAI Mathematics repository lists 719 manuscripts grouped into 372 families as of the public README consulted on 13 October 2026. These figures describe the reference catalogue and do not imply that this monograph has read or independently validated all underlying proofs. Repository content has varied in public versions; manuscript-specific claims should always be checked against their primary texts, available formalizations, citations, and version histories. Formal verification of an encoded theorem is not equivalent to proving that the encoded statement perfectly captures the original informal claim. Likewise, mathematical plausibility, numerical experiments, AI consensus, and persuasive exposition are not substitutes for deductive proof. The work is independent of OpenAI. It does not assert ownership of the original repository manuscripts, certify their correctness, or claim empirical results for the proposed research protocols. Its central contribution is an explicit research architecture in which negative findings, source corrections, independent reproduction, rights boundaries, and the freedom of successor investigators to challenge or replace earlier conclusions are treated as first-class scholarly artifacts. A mathematical civilization is not sustained merely by saving documents. It is sustained when future researchers can reconstruct the precise statement, revisit the evidence, inspect the dependencies, reject an invalid inference, and open a better question. CONCEPTUAL EMERGENCE & GENERATIVE INTELLIGENCE AT THE LIMIT Living Concept Civilization — Flagship Research Monograph 06 STARLI / White Rainbow Civilization · October 2026 ABSTRACT When do interactions among concepts, models, tools and people produce a genuinely new, independently verifiable capacity rather than a novel label or a misleading evaluation threshold? This English-language research monograph develops a falsifiable program for conceptual emergence and generative intelligence. Its research three-coupling is Interaction Generation × New-Function Identification × Counterfactual Verification. The proposed emergence expression compares held-out capability improvement with the strongest viable baseline and a contamination penalty, with all terms requiring operational definition and appropriate normalization before use. RESEARCH DESIGN The volume studies both smooth scaling and possible discontinuities, evaluation-metric sensitivity, training-data leakage, compositional generalization, simple-rule baselines, factorial component ablation, multi-agent collaboration, correlated errors, human-AI complementarity, multimodal grounding, causal interventions, tool-dependence, calibration, cross-model reproducibility, governance, and intergenerational handoff. A claimed capability must survive preregistered unseen tasks, strong comparators, counterfactual perturbations and independent reproduction. A fluent explanation, a generated new term or a model's assertion of consciousness is not evidence of functional emergence. MONOGRAPH STRUCTURE The 82 research chapters each present one distinct proposed chapter-wide operational equation, followed by twelve independently paginated study sections. Thirty advanced physics derivation routes appear in the preface with three-dimensional conceptual diagrams; they are existing physics statements within specified domains and do not establish laws of language or awareness. The concluding 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos each feature one of 233 distinct physical equation anchors. These equations are methodological contrasts and educational prompts, not proof of the emergence hypotheses. A separate Excel workbook indexes chapters, sections, gates, candidate mechanisms and physics anchors. EVIDENCE AND ETHICS This monograph is a theoretical and experimental research agenda. It reports no new trials, controlled effects or validated discoveries; all proposed mechanisms, metrics, forecasts and outcomes are UNVERIFIED until independently tested. The distinction between appearance under a chosen test and a robust new function must be maintained. Consent, intellectual provenance, lawful data use, security and affected persons' right to refuse are hard constraints rather than offsettable penalties. OPEN RESEARCH INVITATION Research Gates reserve space for questions that can be rejected, refined or answered by future researchers. Phoenix Answer Embryos are provisional designs that can be falsified, decomposed, recombined or responsibly retired. The goal is not a permanent claim that machines awaken or that thought obeys physical equations; it is an enduring, contestable toolkit for recognizing and scrutinizing useful new functions.
